text.p: - Anatoly Chubais, appointed first deputy prime minister last Friday, is expected to implement an early crackdown on Russia's acute housing problems. State subsidies for communal services are likely to be cut significantly.
Liquidating redundant and inefficient structures in the Russian army would help finance long-expected military reform.
- When Russia and NATO really reach agreement, Moscow will have to face the difficult task of quelling opposition at home.
- Atomic Energy minister Viktor Mikhailov says Russia no longer has nuclear warheads in Ukraine, Belarus or Kazakhstan, and half Russia's nuclear arsenal has been destroyed.
- Anatoly Chubais is planning to entirely reshuffle the government to bring a new political and economic elite to power.
- Russia may expect a new economic shock with the return of Anatoly Chubais to the government.
- President Yeltsin appointed Anatoly Chubais to a key position in the government regardless of public opinion.

- Ordinary Russians support the ideas expressed by the president in his annual address to parliament, says the paper published by Yeltsin's administration. -- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
